title: Memory store schemas + migrations: session_memories + memories (embedded, HNSW), tenant/subject scoped
priority_note: Foundation story — every other epic_28 story depends on these tables. No dependencies of its own.

background.reference: GitHub issue #307; Second Brain hub 3ee5f890 (Cole Medin agent-memory pillar); revived idea 787761cd. Enhanced-review round 1 (analyst/architect/adversarial) findings applied.
background.includes: loopctl's Knowledge Wiki stores curated articles (articles table, pgvector embeddings, HNSW index). There is NO per-agent working-memory concept; mcp-memory-keeper (separate repo, flat JSON) is the current stand-in. This story adds the persistence substrate for a native memory subsystem, kept strictly separate from the knowledge tables. pgvector is already enabled by migration 20260410022854. NOTE: loopctl is agent-native — API-key auth only, no human web UI — so scope owners are API-key identities, not human users.

story.i_want_to: add two Ecto schemas and migrations — session_memories (short-term append log with expiry, not embedded) and memories (long-term, embedded vector(1536) + HNSW cosine index) — each scoped by tenant_id + project_id + subject_id
story.so_that: agents have a durable, scoped place to write and later semantically recall memory without overloading the curated-knowledge articles table

rationale: Cole Medin's production architecture names agent memory as a non-optional pillar: short-term session memory plus a per-user long-term memory retrieved by vector search that scales to millions of entries. The Knowledge Wiki is the wrong home for this (different lifecycle, agent-private not curated), so a dedicated scoped schema is the precondition for the context module, API, and MCP tools in the rest of the epic. The scope model (subject_id) is the subsystem's security boundary and must be pinned precisely at the schema layer.

acceptance_criteria.description: Schema Loopctl.Memory.SessionMemory (table session_memories): fields session_id :string (required), tenant_id, project_id (nullable), subject_id :string (scope owner, required), role Ecto.Enum [:user,:assistant,:system,:fact], content :text, metadata :map, expires_at :utc_datetime_usec (required), inserted_at. Append-only, no embedding column. Composite index on (tenant_id, session_id, inserted_at) for chronological read and an index on expires_at for pruning.

Schema Loopctl.Memory.Memory (table memories): fields tenant_id, project_id (nullable), subject_id :string (scope owner, required), text :text (required), embedding Pgvector.Ecto.Vector with load_in_query: false, embedding_content_hash :string, confidence :float default 1.0, source Ecto.Enum [:explicit,:promoted] default :explicit, source_session_id (nullable), tags {:array,:string} default [], superseded_by (nullable self-reference to memories, references with on_delete: :nilify_all), inserted_at, updated_at.

Migration creates an HNSW cosine index on memories.embedding using the existing lib/loopctl/repo/hnsw_index.ex helper (mirroring 20260410022906_add_embedding_hnsw_index.exs), and a btree index on (tenant_id, subject_id) to back scope filtering on the OLTP path. The HNSW index is asserted present by capability (pg_am amname = 'hnsw'), never by a hard-coded name (tolerating prod name drift, same foot-gun as US-27.1 AC-27.1.7).

subject_id derivation is pinned and total: it is resolved server-side from the caller's API key — api_key.agent_id for agent-role keys, else api_key.id — and is NEVER accepted from request params. Because Loopctl.Auth.Role ranks agent as the FLOOR role (level 1), every authenticated key resolves to a non-null subject_id via this rule; if resolution ever yields nil the changeset/caller path returns an error rather than persisting a null-scoped (leak-prone) row. tenant_id and subject_id are set programmatically, never via cast.

Changesets validate required fields (session_id, subject_id, tenant_id, text/content, expires_at for session) and cap text/content byte length; over-cap text and missing scope both produce changeset errors.

Tenant isolation on the OLTP path (writes, list, forget via Loopctl.Repo) rides the same RLS/SetTenant mechanism as articles. NOTE for downstream stories: the semantic recall path (US-28.2) runs on Loopctl.HeavyReadRepo which is BYPASSRLS, so recall isolation is NOT RLS — it is an explicit (tenant_id, subject_id) predicate enforced by a structural guard (US-28.2 AC). This AC documents the split so no implementer assumes RLS covers recall.
Down migrations drop both tables, the HNSW index, and the btree indexes with no orphaned index or enum type; migrations run green on a fresh DB and pass the project's migration/rollback test.

test_cases.name: Both tables exist with expected columns and an HNSW index on memories.embedding
preconditions: migrations run on a fresh test database
steps: Query information_schema.columns for session_memories and memories
Query pg_indexes joined to pg_am for an hnsw index on memories.embedding
Query pg_indexes for the (tenant_id, subject_id) btree on memories
expected_results: All columns from AC-28.1.1 and AC-28.1.2 are present with the specified types (including expires_at, subject_id, superseded_by)
An HNSW index on memories.embedding is detected via pg_am amname = 'hnsw'

test_cases.name: Memory changeset rejects a row with no resolved subject scope
steps: Build Loopctl.Memory.Memory changeset with text set but subject_id resolved to nil (simulating a key with nil agent_id and no fallback)
expected_results: errors include subject_id (and tenant_id when absent)

test_cases.name: Over-cap text is rejected by the changeset
steps: Build a Memory changeset with text exceeding the byte-length cap under a valid scope
expected_results: changeset.valid? == false with a length error on text

test_cases.name: superseded_by nilifies when the referenced memory is deleted
preconditions: a = fixture(:memory, tenant: tenant, subject_id: "A", text: "old")
b = fixture(:memory, tenant: tenant, subject_id: "A", text: "new")
expected_results: a.superseded_by is nil (on_delete: :nilify_all), so a is not left pointing at a deleted row

test_cases.name: Memory rows are tenant-isolated on the OLTP path
preconditions: insert one memory under tenant_a via the scoped changeset
steps: List memories in tenant_b scope via Loopctl.Repo
List memories in tenant_a scope via Loopctl.Repo
expected_results: tenant_id/subject_id were set programmatically, not from cast params

technical_notes: Namespace: Loopctl.Memory.* (domain) — a sibling to Loopctl.Knowledge.*, NOT nested under it.
Schema modules: Loopctl.Memory.SessionMemory, Loopctl.Memory.Memory. Tables: session_memories, memories.
Reuse Pgvector.Ecto.Vector with load_in_query: false exactly as lib/loopctl/knowledge/article.ex (line ~63) does; dimension 1536.
HNSW: reuse lib/loopctl/repo/hnsw_index.ex; detect by pg_am amname = 'hnsw' to tolerate name drift.

subject_id is a STRING holding the resolved API-key identity (api_key.agent_id for agent keys, else api_key.id). agent_id is :binary_id and nullable in lib/loopctl/auth/api_key.ex; the fallback to api_key.id is what makes AC-28.1.4 total. This is the security boundary — see US-28.2/US-28.3 for the structural guard + tests.
superseded_by references memories with on_delete: :nilify_all so forget/2 (US-28.2) never leaves a memory permanently hidden behind a dangling pointer.
session_memories carries expires_at; the prune worker + TTL policy live in US-28.2. #307 requires Part 1 to bound session memory.
embedding is NULL on insert; populated asynchronously by the worker in US-28.2 — do not block writes on embedding.
source enum includes :promoted now (written by #308's compiler in Part 2) so Part 2 needs no migration.

Tests use Loopctl.Fixtures.fixture/1,2; add fixture(:memory, attrs) and fixture(:session_memory, attrs) helpers in this story. fixture(:tenant) and fixture(:api_key, role:) already exist; there is NO fixture(:user)/fixture(:tenant_user) (no human-auth in loopctl).
